title: Check that athena.toml and defaults.toml parse during admission
summary: Today the gate's "configuration parses" check (content.rs) only runs at landing. The reading adds the same check to candidate admission in athena-core, where secrets are already scanned. A candidate whose athena.toml or defaults.toml has an unknown field then fails with a repairable finding before the landing commit is built. A test covers an unknown field. The audience is the Athena operator and the producer agent that reads the finding.

defaults_applied.how: The change and its tests are Rust.
The new tests cover an unknown field in each of the two files; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change in admission.rs, with at most a changelog line.
The candidate is checked at admission using the real parsers, rather than catching one unknown-field case by hand.
It reuses Config::parse and DefaultsModel::parse, so no new parser or schema is built.
Behavior criteria name the cargo test commands the verifier can run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: "During verification" means candidate admission in crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs, which run.rs calls before fingerprinting and the verifier checks. Admission already scans for secrets there "so a secret fails the job here instead of at landing". I did not take it to mean a configured [capabilities.change] check command, because that would mean editing athena.toml, a governance file.
The gate's own check in athena-gate/src/content.rs stays as the landing-time backstop. Admission reuses the same parsers rather than a new schema.
The finding goes through PolicyViolation (rule, path, detail), which has no separate repair field. The repair text goes into the detail, for example "fix the file so it parses".
Only a changed athena.toml or defaults.toml is parsed, using the candidate's blob. Whether the check also repeats the exempt-commit rule is left to the producer. Parsing alone meets the request.
The test uses Git::isolated with a temporary repository, as other athena-core tests do.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs builds a base commit and a candidate commit whose athena.toml contains an unknown field. admit() must return a violation with rule "configuration", the path athena.toml, and a detail that names the parse error and says how to repair it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.

A second test covers an unknown field in defaults.toml: admit() returns a configuration violation for the path defaults.toml. A third test shows that a candidate whose athena.toml and defaults.toml both parse, and a candidate that touches neither file, add no configuration violation. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.

admit() parses the candidate's athena.toml and defaults.toml only when they changed, using Config::parse and DefaultsModel::parse from athena-data (the same parsers the gate uses). It does not duplicate the schema. A deleted file is not parsed. The violation reaches the existing candidate.violations path in run.rs, so the job is rejected with the finding before landing.
The module doc comment in admission.rs lists the new rule. A parse failure is reported as an admission violation (the finding), not as an anyhow error that aborts the job.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, including the existing athena-gate content tests for the configuration rule.

out_of_scope: Changing the gate's landing-time checks or the Rule enum names
Editing athena.toml or defaults.toml, including adding a check entry to [capabilities.change]
Changing the config schema or adding fields
The exempt-commit history validation in content.rs::new_exemptions
Validating other files, such as roles.toml or Cargo.toml
departures: None beyond the reference. The change is small and has a clear precedent in admission's secrets scan, but "as a check during verification" could mean a configured check, and that risk lowers acceptance a little.
